newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia central bank chief says banks recovering.
newsitem.headline: Latvia central bank chief says banks recovering.

text.p: Latvian central bank chief Einar Repshe said on Wednesday that the Baltic state's banking sector was stabilising and strengthening after last year's bank crisis and that its growth would continue to be steady.

Latvia's banking sector saw rapid expansion after the collapse of the former Soviet Union but its contraction was just as swift after the collapse of what was the largest bank, Banka Baltiya, in the middle of 1995.
Repshe said banks had emerged stronger from the crisis.
"We will continue to build the banking system through steady and orderly growth," he told a banking conference.
"The banking system is continuing to stabilise and indeed in recent months it has strengthened," Repshe added.
Latvia's central bank set new auditing and supervisory rules to control the bank sector and weed out weak banks.
He said the banks now had better internal controls, regular international audits and also accepted the need for tougher supervision by the authorities.

Central bank deputy head Ilmars Rimshevich said the recovery in the sector was witnessed by the fact that banks made a cumulative profit of 17 million lats in the first half of 1996, deposits rose by 10 percent, assets by 12 percent and own capital by 24 percent.
